data.title: Bitcoin, crypto stocks slip as hopes for Clarity Act progress fade
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fell as much as 4.9% on Tuesday from Monday's high of nearly $80K after a Democratic counteroffer over the Clarity Act dimmed hopes of the digital asset legislation progressing.

The price of the largest cryptocurrency by market cap slid to $76.6K Tuesday afternoon, down 3.0% over the past 24 hours. The low of the day was $75.7K, compared with Monday's high-level mark of $79.6K.

Ethereum (ETH-USD), the second-largest digital token by market cap, dropped 3.9% to $2.44K.

The odds of the Clarity Act becoming law before Jan. 1, 2027, slid to 13% from as high as 39% at 7:27 AM ET. Legislators have been squabbling over the stablecoin legislation for about a year.

A procedural vote to advance the bill to the Senate floor for a full vote is due to take place Tuesday afternoon. Major sticking points included ethics over legislators and the president profiting from stablecoins and other digital assets and whether platforms should be allowed to pay interest on stablecoin holdings.

Cryptocurrencies and crypto stocks climbed on Monday after Republicans' final draft of the legislation included some ethics restrictions on conflicts of interest. It would also give the Treasury Department authority to intervene if deposit flight started to hurt community banks, according to media reports.

The Federal Reserve's rate decision, to be announced on Wednesday, may also have investors wary of risk assets, including crypto. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee is widely expected to increase its policy rate by 25 basis points, its first hike since 2023.

Crypto stocks slumping the most in Tuesday trading include Circle Internet (CRCL) -11%, Coinbase Global (COIN) -9.2%, Gemini Space Station (GEMI) -8.6%, and Bakkt (BKKT) -7.1%. Crypto mining stocks also dipped: Riot Platforms (RIOT) -5.9%, CleanSpark (CLSK) -5.6%, Core Scientific (CORZ) -4.8%, Hut 8 (HUT) -4.4%, and IREN (IREN) -4.4%.

data.title: 20-year Treasury auction hits record yield as foreign demand plunges
data.description:
The 20-year U.S. Treasury bond (US20Y) (TLT) auction Tuesday revealed market hesitation as foreign demand plummeted.

The $13B auction's 5.420% high yield marks the highest level for the 20-year tenor since its May 2020 reintroduction, up from August’s 5.204%, as long-dated yields keep hitting multi-year highs.

Underscoring the notably soft demand, the final yield tailed the when-issued level of 5.400% by a wide 2.0 basis points—the largest such tail seen since 2024, according to Zerohedge. Furthermore, while the bid-to-cover ratio edged up slightly to 2.57 from last month’s 2.53, it remained sluggish compared with the recent historical average of 2.65.

What's more, indirect bidders, typically a proxy for international investors and foreign central banks, took down a meager 52.5% of the offering. This represents a steep plunge from the previous 62.9% and falls short of the 68.0% recent average, Zerohedge pointed out.

To compensate for the fleeing international capital, domestic participants had to step up. Direct bidders absorbed a record-shattering 30.7% of the auction, surging from 24.6% previously. Consequently, primary dealers were left holding a hefty 16.9% of the supply. Ultimately, the near-record dealer burden emphasizes the growing challenge of finding willing buyers for long-duration government debt without offering significant yield premiums.

The dismal auction arrives against a punishing backdrop for government debt, extending a broader trend of elevated long-term Treasury yields as markets endure a persistent global bond selloff in the face of growing concerns about surging energy prices, rising debt and inflation. Ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision Wednesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) (IEF) climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, testing the 5% mark.

data.title: Enbridge upgraded at BMO on recent pullback, improving growth visibility
data.description:
Enbridge (ENB) gains 0.6% in Tuesday's trading as BMO Capital upgraded the pipeline operator to Outperform from Market Perform with a C$79.50 price target, saying the stock's recent pullback and improving visibility on growth make an attractive investment in a choppy macroeconomic environment.

Enbridge (ENB) shares have underperformed Canadian midstream and pipeline peers YTD, likely due to rising bond yields, lack of visibility on the company's ~5% growth guidance through the end of the decade, and a recent equity offering, while peers sport higher perceived growth rates, BMO's Ben Pham said.

The analyst said Enbridge (ENB) operates more like a diversified utility, prioritizing premium long-duration contracted assets over higher beta abnormal growth, and believes the company's scale, limited commodity exposure, and diversified assets are underappreciated.

"Few companies can boast a visible premium organic growth program like Enbridge, with its $41B in the secured backlog and $20B of new projects expected to be sanctioned in 2026-27," Pham wrote, while opportunistic acquisitions such as Salt Creek Midstream and the Tallgrass crude transport business come with embedded future upside.

Enbridge's (ENB) ~$3B equity offering and innovative $2.7B joint venture with KKR on its Westcoast B.C. pipeline have shored up the balance sheet, providing additional financial flexibility to fund new growth opportunities that could arise, the analyst said.

data.title: AI chip rally breaks the software–semi link
data.description:
Software delivered its strongest single-day showing versus semiconductors in roughly 25 years on Monday. 

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) advanced +5%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) declined about -5.7%, a spread that reversed the pattern that has defined much of the artificial intelligence cycle.

That cycle had already strained a historically tight link between the two groups. Chipmakers powered the AI build-out and left software far behind, driving their two-year correlation to an unusually weak level. Hardware captured the first wave of capital; application software lagged as investors treated it as a delayed beneficiary—or even a disruption risk. 

Growing debate over whether AI infrastructure spending can keep its recent pace now puts that gap in a different light. A rotation from semiconductors toward lagging software would not require a new bull market in IGV. Even a partial unwind of the extreme relative move could produce meaningful outperformance.

data.title: Novo CEO seeks a more consumer-centric culture from employees
data.description:
Close on the heels of a major rebranding exercise, Novo Nordisk's (NVO) CEO Mike Doustdar on Tuesday urged his employees to be more consumer-focused as the weight-loss drugmaker attempts to regain market share lost to rival Eli Lilly (LLY).

"We would like to become a ​better and a bigger company. A company ​that ⁠does more for many more, both patients and consumers," said Doustdar during a town hall meeting at the company's headquarters ‌near ⁠Copenhagen, Denmark.

His remarks came a day after the Danish drugmaker unveiled a major rebranding drive centered on a single ‘Novo’ name and a revamped culture identified as ‘The Novo Way.’

“Healthcare must become more responsive, relevant, and easier to fit into everyday life,” Doustdar said as he announced the company's new corporate identity on Monday, roughly a year after becoming its CEO.

It’s the company’s latest effort to regain control of the lucrative GLP-1 drug market, where Lilly (LLY) has taken control despite Novo’s (NVO) first-mover advantage.

data.title: Domestic lithium supply chain: Projects vs. promises
data.description:
Investors Should Know: The push to build domestic critical-mineral supply chains has moved from policy discussion to active construction and permitting, with lithium at the center of the effort. A small group of U.S.-focused developers and recyclers are advancing projects with federal backing, but the gap between a defined project and a financed, producing one remains the defining risk across the sector.

Key Takeaways

  • Domestic lithium development is progressing along two distinct tracks: construction-stage projects with secured financing and earlier-stage developers still working through permitting, funding, and final investment decisions.
  • U.S. industrial policy is creating a two-sided dynamic for domestic critical-mineral companies: federal support and permitting streamlining can improve long-term positioning, but shifting export and processing rules can disrupt near-term commercialization.
  • Supply-chain resilience requires more than new mining capacity. Analysts emphasize that refining and processing infrastructure are equally critical bottlenecks, and domestic developers that address the full chain carry a different strategic profile than pure extractors.
  • Broader metals exposure through diversified mining ETFs offers a different risk profile than single-project lithium developers, though it also reduces direct exposure to any one lithium supply story.
  • Analyst sentiment on individual names is mixed, with quantitative ratings and analyst-driven ratings often pointing in opposite directions. This divergence that reflects the gap between near-term financial metrics and longer-term strategic positioning.

Background: Building a Domestic Critical-Mineral Supply Chain

Lithium and other critical minerals sit at the foundation of electric vehicles, grid-scale batteries, and a range of defense and industrial applications. For years, the refining and processing of these materials have been concentrated outside the United States, creating supply-chain dependencies that have drawn increasing attention from policymakers.

The response has taken the form of federal grants, loan programs, permitting priority designations, and policy frameworks designed to accelerate domestic development. The challenge is that building a complete domestic ecosystem, covering mining, processing, refining, and end-use manufacturing. This is a multi-year, capital-intensive undertaking.

The sector distinction that matters most for investors relates to whether it has the financing, permits, and processing capability to bring that resource to market.

Stocks to Watch: LAC, SLI, ABAT

Lithium Americas Corp. (LAC) is a lithium developer whose flagship Thacker Pass project in Nevada is currently under construction, making it among the most advanced domestic lithium development projects in the publicly traded space. Standard Lithium Ltd. (SLI) is a lithium developer focused on the Smackover formation in Arkansas, where it is advancing toward a final investment decision in partnership with a major industry player.

American Battery Technology Company (ABAT) takes a more integrated approach, combining domestic lithium-resource development with battery recycling operations and mineral processing capabilities. Broader metals exposure is available through exchange-traded funds including SPDR S&P Metals and Mining ETF (XME), iShares Copper and Metals Mining ETF (ICOP), and iShares MSCI Global Metals and Mining Producers ETF (PICK).

News Roundup

  • J.P. Morgan upgraded Lithium Americas (LAC) to Overweight, citing improved long-term lithium assumptions, confidence in Thacker Pass execution, and continued U.S. policy support for domestic critical-mineral supply. At the time of the report, engineering was more than 95% complete and procurement more than 80% complete.
  • American Battery Technology Company reported progress on a second recycling facility backed by a $150 million U.S. Department of Energy grant, alongside a separate $10 million grant supporting critical-mineral processing technologies.
  • ABAT also announced reinstatement of a $57.7 million Department of Energy cooperative agreement for its Tonopah Flats lithium project, completion of baseline environmental studies, and acceptance of its Plan of Operations by the Bureau of Land Management. The project received Priority Project designations intended to streamline federal permitting.
  • Standard Lithium is approaching a final investment decision for its Arkansas project, with a potential U.S. government grant and possible bank funding associated with the Smackover Lithium joint venture under discussion.

What Analysts Say

Analyst coverage of domestic critical-mineral names skews cautiously constructive, with most bullish arguments centered on policy tailwinds, project advancement milestones, and strategic positioning rather than current financial performance. Bears and quantitative models tend to flag execution risk, negative returns on equity, and reliance on external financing as the key near-term concerns.

The divergence between author ratings and quantitative ratings is particularly notable in this space. Several names carry strong author or sell-side ratings alongside weak or negative quantitative scores, reflecting the tension between long-term strategic thesis and near-term financial metrics.

Analyst Commentary

Austin Craig: Standard Lithium Ltd. (SLI) — Craig frames SLI as a cash-rich and asset-rich developer nearing a critical milestone, with a final investment decision for the Arkansas project and potential government grant and bank funding for the Smackover Lithium joint venture as the key near-term catalysts. The central argument is that funding progress could materially strengthen the company's position, with the broader strategic rationale tied to reducing Western dependence on Chinese mineral refining. Read more

The Sharpe Quest: American Battery Technology Company (ABAT) — The Sharpe Quest characterizes ABAT's latest quarter as operationally stronger but highlights ongoing regulatory risk from black-mass export restrictions and continued reliance on at-the-market financing. The thesis is that the same industrial policy creating a near-term constraint could ultimately benefit ABAT by driving demand for domestic refining capacity. Read more

Grassroots Trading: SPDR S&P Metals and Mining ETF (XME) — Grassroots Trading rates XME Buy and argues that U.S. trade policy, domestic industrial support, and strategic-mineral policy are important drivers for the fund. The analysis cautions that the ETF's underlying exposure skews toward steel, gold, and coal rather than copper, and that higher protected prices can eventually weigh on downstream demand. Read more

Andrew Hecht: iShares Copper and Metals Mining ETF (ICOP) — Hecht rates ICOP Buy, pointing to electrification trends, data-center investment, and constrained production growth as demand supports for copper and base metals. He notes that mining shares can be more volatile than the underlying metals, as company profitability is sensitive to the spread between commodity prices and production costs. Read more

data.title: Cellectis falls as Citizens downgrades on pivot to genetic medicines
data.description:
Cellectis (CLLS) ADRs continued to drop for the second straight session on Tuesday as Citizens Capital Markets downgraded the French biotech, citing its decision to prioritize its in vivo gene editing therapies over CAR-T cell therapies.

The Paris-based company traded sharply lower on Monday after unveiling a strategic transformation to focus on its in vivo gene editing candidates, HEAL-101 and HEAL-201, targeted at cardiovascular diseases.

Concurrently, the company announced plans to discontinue the development of CAR-T cell therapies lasme-cel and eti-cel, a decision that could delay related clinical catalysts to late 2027/2028, according to Citizens Analyst Silvan Turkcan.

"We are bullish on genetic medicines for CVD and believe CLLS may provide a unique approach, but clinical catalysts have been pushed back to late 2027/2028, and early biomarkers may not be very helpful in de-risking a program," wrote Turkcan.

With Cellectis (CLLS) shares trading at roughly a 28% discount to its $169M worth of cash reserves, the analyst argued the company is fairly valued in line with its biotech peers encountering similar uncertainties. Turkcan downgraded the stock to Market Perform from Market Outperform.

data.title: Two Robinhood employees charged with fraud over misappropriating insider information
data.description:
U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York, charged two Robinhood (HOOD) (HOOD:CA) employees with fraud.

Robinhood engineers Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang were charged with commodities fraud and wire fraud arising from a scheme to misappropriate confidential business information from their employer.

The information was allegedly used to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized derivatives exchange, Hyperliquid.

According to the complaint filed in the Manhattan federal court, Chai and Xiang had access to nonpublic information related to whether and when Robinhood will support additional cryptocurrencies for trading on a subsidiary digital asset trading platform.

"Today's charges make clear that corporate insiders cannot evade the securities and commodities laws by trading based on misappropriated information in derivatives like perpetual futures, tokenized securities, or other similar financial instruments," said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.

data.title: BHP Port Hedland workers to seek arbitration in labor dispute, union says
data.description:
Workers at BHP's (BHP) ‌Port Hedland facility in Australia will pursue arbitration after the two sides failed to reach terms on a new wage deal, the Combined BHP Ports Unions said Tuesday, according to Reuters.

The union, which represents ~450 operators and maintenance workers at Port Hedland, will apply for an intractable bargaining declaration, which ​allows Australia's Fair Work Commission to set terms for ⁠the ⁠agreement.

BHP (BHP) has offered ​a 17% pay increase for most workers over the four years of the ​agreement, which ⁠will include a A$25K transition payment over two years, as well as an increase to roster allowances, but the union argues that ~40% of the workforce would be worse off under the company's proposal.

BHP (BHP) is "unwilling to negotiate an agreement that reflects the specialized skills, extreme conditions and significant ‌personal sacrifices ⁠of the people who generated the company more than $13 billion in profit this year," the union said in a statement.

Port Hedland is the world's ⁠largest ⁠iron ore export hub and the main shipping gateway for ​BHP's (BHP) Pilbara operations.

data.title: Undervalued healthcare stocks with attractive valuation grades

With valuations varying significantly across the sector, stocks trading at discounts to their underlying fundamentals can offer potentially attractive opportunities for investors.

Below is a list of the top 11 healthcare stocks ranked by their quantitative Valuation Grade.
